title: 1975 AHSME Problem 9
statement: Let \(a_1,\) \(a_2,\) \(\ldots\) and \(b_1,\) \(b_2,\) \(\ldots\) be arithmetic progressions such that \(a_1=25,\) \(b_1=75,\) and \(a_{100}+b_{100}=100.\) Find the sum of the first one hundred terms of the progression \(a_1+b_1,\) \(a_2+b_2,\) \(\ldots.\)

answerChoices.label: E
answerChoices.text: not enough information given to solve the problem

solutions.text:
Let \(c_i=a_i+b_i.\) This is an arithmetic progression with \(c_1=25+75=100\) and \(c_{100}=100.\) Equal endpoint terms force its common difference to be \(0,\) so all \(100\) terms equal \(100.\) Their sum is \(10{,}000.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is C.

Its first and hundredth terms are both \(100\)
